_readme: Golden evaluation dataset. DATA, NOT CODE — add a case by editing this file.
case_id is STABLE AND IMMUTABLE. Provider comparisons join historical runs on
it, so renaming or renumbering one silently disconnects every past result that
referenced it. Add new ids freely; never reuse or rewrite an existing one.
A test pins the known ids: additions pass, renames and removals fail.
Ids read <capability-short>-<nnn>. The number is a counter, not a rank.
Every case must be a FAITHFUL reproduction of a real call: the same capability
and the same `variables` a capability service passes. `expected_output` must
satisfy that capability's real production schema — the loader validates this
and refuses to load a dataset that does not.
difficulty: trivial | typical | hard  — how much judgement a correct answer
needs, NOT how long the prompt is.
category: free text, used to slice a run afterwards.

cases.description: Plain question about one candidate, fully answerable from the supplied context.

variables.context: Candidate: Priya Raman. Role: Senior Backend Engineer. ATS score 82. Eight years in payments infrastructure. Skills: Python, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes. Notable: rebuilt a ledger service to 40k writes/sec.
variables.question: Is this candidate a fit for a senior backend role?

expected_output.answer: Priya Raman is a strong fit for a senior backend role. Eight years in payments infrastructure and a ledger rebuilt to 40k writes/sec are directly relevant to the requirement.
expected_output.summary: Strong fit — deep payments and distributed-systems experience.
strengths: Core stack matches: Python, PostgreSQL, Kafka
weaknesses: No evidence of frontend or full-stack breadth
recommendations: Probe the ledger rebuild for depth of ownership
expected_output.reasoning_summary: Grounded in the candidate record and résumé supplied in context.
followups: What were the failure modes of the ledger rebuild?
How does she compare to the other shortlisted candidates?

cases.description: Question the supplied context cannot answer — the honest reply is to say so, not to guess.

variables.context: Candidate: Priya Raman. Role: Senior Backend Engineer. ATS score 82.
variables.question: What were her salary expectations in her last role?

expected_output.answer: The candidate record does not contain salary expectations, so I cannot answer that from your data.
expected_output.summary: Not answerable from the available sources.
recommendations: Record compensation expectations on the candidate profile
expected_output.reasoning_summary: No compensation data in the supplied context.
followups: What is in her record today?

cases.description: Explanation layer over a deterministic ATS score. The model must explain, never re-score.

variables.resume_json: {"name": "Priya Raman", "skills": ["Python", "PostgreSQL", "Kafka", "Kubernetes"], "experience": [{"role": "Senior Backend Engineer", "company": "Ledgerworks", "description": ["Rebuilt the core ledger to sustain 40k writes/sec"]}], "education": [{"degree": "BE Computer Science", "institution": "Anna University"}]}

expected_output.candidate_summary: A senior backend engineer with eight years in payments infrastructure, strongest in high-throughput data systems. The résumé is well structured and keyword-dense for backend roles.
career_recommendations: Add measurable outcomes to every role, not just the most recent
Include links to talks or open-source work
expected_output.interview_readiness: Ready for a senior systems-design interview; prepare depth on the ledger rebuild.

cases.description: Résumé against a JD with a genuine gap, so missing_skills must not be empty.

variables.job_description: Senior Backend Engineer. Required: Python, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, and production experience with Go. Nice to have: Kafka.
variables.resume_json: {"name": "Priya Raman", "skills": ["Python", "PostgreSQL", "Kafka", "Kubernetes"], "experience": [{"role": "Senior Backend Engineer", "company": "Ledgerworks", "description": ["Rebuilt the core ledger to sustain 40k writes/sec"]}]}

expected_output.experience_relevance: Highly relevant: eight years of backend work with direct high-throughput ledger ownership.
candidate_strengths: Stack overlap on three of four required skills
areas_for_improvement: No exposure to the team's Go services
expected_output.recommendation_explanation: Strong on three of four required skills; the Go gap is the only substantive risk and is learnable for an engineer at this level.

cases.description: Prioritise detected pipeline situations into a recruiter briefing.

variables.situations:
- [urgent] Offer expiring in 24h — Priya Raman has an unaccepted offer expiring tomorrow
- [high] Stalled candidate — Arun Mehta has been in Interview for 14 days with no activity
- [medium] Unreviewed pile — 12 new candidates on Senior Backend Engineer

expected_output.headline: 3 items need attention, 1 urgent
priorities: Chase the expiring offer for Priya Raman
Review the 12 new Senior Backend Engineer candidates
expected_output.summary: One offer expires within 24 hours and is the only irreversible item; the stalled interview is the next-most costly to leave. The unreviewed pile is routine.
